q: In October so far, what was our best day and our worst day for profit, and what was different about them?

answer:
Best day (highest net profit): 2026-10-27 — Net profit ₹3,875.39. Worst day (lowest net profit): 2026-10-09 — Net profit −₹26,445.47. These are by order date.

What moved and why it matters
- 2026-10-09 (worst): Net profit fell to −₹26,445 from a more normal weekday level (the modelled “usual” was around −₹16,711). The drop was driven by a large P&L ad‑spend line (ad spend (P&L basis) ₹60,101.69) combined with lower contribution margin (contribution margin ₹33,656.22). In short: advertising cost stayed high while the revenue and contribution that would cover it were down, so profit plunged.
- 2026-10-27 (best): Net profit rose to ₹3,875.39 from the prior day's −₹5,369 mainly because contribution margin increased sharply (to ₹47,327.14) while P&L ad spend rose too but by less in proportion (ad spend (P&L basis) ₹43,451.76). Net sales (P&L basis) jumped (to ₹75,932.57), so the business covered ad spend and produced a positive net profit.
- Where the changes concentrated: the diagnostics localise the worst-day swing around a small set of ad elements (specific ad and campaign ids noted in the analysis) that moved materially versus their usual levels; the best-day gain similarly concentrated in a handful of ads/adsets that produced most of the uplift in contribution margin.

Worth checking:
- For 2026-10-09: which campaigns/ads ran that day (the campaign/ad ids flagged) and whether any bid/budget changes or creatives launched — they account for a large share of the negative swing.
- For 2026-10-27: which products/orders increased contribution margin (see the contribution lines) and whether that was broad or concentrated in a few SKUs or campaigns.
